summary: Backend + frontend validation of the Multi-Specialist Network: Founder onboarding, email activation flow, portal doctor directory with per-doctor clinics/services/slots, auto-created child record at a new specialist on booking, and parent-signed sharing consent (plus read-only linked-specialists view on the doctor passport). 15/15 pytest cases pass. Frontend admin add-specialist form, Doctors list (status badge + resend + network toggle), parent booking dialog with doctor selector cascading to clinic + services + slots, and share card (active state + revoke) all show the expected data-testids and work on both desktop (1920) and mobile (390).

minor.issue: Spec says invited doctor should receive 403 'Account non ancora attivato' but current implementation verifies password BEFORE status, so any attempt with the unknown random seed password returns 401 'Email o password non corretti'. The invited doctor is still effectively locked out, but the error message is misleading. Fix: call ensure_active(user) before verify_password() in auth.py login handler.

The founder invite flow calls send_email synchronously inside the request handler. For @example.com destinations the SMTP provider sometimes takes >60s and the Cloudflare ingress returns 502 Bad Gateway even though the doctor is created server-side. Consider moving send_email to a BackgroundTask so the API returns within the ingress budget regardless of SMTP latency.

issues: Dev-mode debug wrapper injects <span> inside <option> which produces a React hydration warning ('In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>'). Does not affect functionality — options render and are selectable — but shows a noisy console warning on every open. Likely coming from the Emergent IDE debug overlay, not from app code.

action_items: Reorder auth.py login: ensure_active(user) BEFORE verify_password() so invited/pending/suspended accounts always get 403 with the explanatory message (matches the spec).
Move send_email() calls out of the request path in network.create_doctor and network.resend_invite (BackgroundTasks / fire-and-forget) to avoid 502s on slow SMTP for @example.com addresses.
critical_code_review_comments: network.py create_doctor: catches generic Exception around send_invite and returns {invited:false} but the HTTPException branch re-raises; however when send_email hangs long enough to cross the ingress timeout, the FastAPI handler never returns and the client sees 502 — the fallback does not help. Prefer BackgroundTasks.

auth.py login order: ensure_active is called AFTER verify_password, so invited doctors cannot distinguish an unactivated account from a wrong password. Suggest swap order (same also for pending/suspended).
scheduling.put_schedule enforces unique service and clinic names via Pydantic validators (good) and requires hours for every clinic. network.create_doctor also enforces unique clinic names (good).
portal_flow.child_at correctly dedupes by cf_hash so repeated bookings at the same new specialist reuse the auto-created record; the user.children list grows once per (owner_id). Good.

network.active_share uses $elemMatch on members (owner_id + patient_id) and shared_pdf verifies the consultation's owner_id is in members and != requesting user — safely blocks fetching own report through the shared endpoint. Verified by test.

RequestDialog relies on net.length ? net : fallback = kid.doctor; if portalNetwork() fails silently the parent sees only their main doctor. The fallback is a sensible UX but should surface a toast on network error.

rca of the issue: Login 401 vs 403 discrepancy for invited doctors — root cause: auth.login() in /app/backend/auth.py line 150 calls `verify_password(body.password, user['password_hash'])` before `ensure_active(user)`. Because create_doctor seeds `password_hash = hash_password(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))` the comparison always fails for the invited doctor → 401. Fix: swap order so ensure_active runs first when a user with that email exists. 502 on admin create/resend — root cause: send_email is awaited inside the HTTP handler; if SMTP latency exceeds the Cloudflare ingress limit the client sees 502 even though the DB mutation and (eventually) the email succeed. Fix: BackgroundTasks.
